who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), port lane for blaze-item-hash, hir and blaze-lower onto blaze-memo, port-memo-1113
what: Which tracked queries are an item's boundary and how each answers was written twice: a list of kind names that mark_boundaries marked, and a separate match in fact_of that turned a read back into a fact. A query that was private to its crate could not be named at all, so 57 of the lane's errors were the two lists losing sync with what hir-def and hir-ty export.
cost: a whole port of reads.rs and two kinds modules, and E0603/E0624 errors across the crate
cause: a query's identity outside its crate is a string path (KIND_NAME), and nothing ties the kind that is marked to the rule that answers it
class: two hand-kept lists that must agree on the same set, keyed by names rather than by the item
prevention: one table, BOUNDARIES, where each row is the query type itself (its KIND_NAME and its key_of) together with its answer; mark_boundaries and fact_of both read it; a test checks every row is named once and that a recorded step has no unmarked or unanswered boundary row
workaround: none needed: built as the prevention
